security_spec.violation_condition: When msdcfg.SIDN holds a value that does not correspond to an implemented supervisor interrupt domain, the XiangShan RTL accesses internal per-domain register arrays (hgeip/hgeie array, IMSIC interrupt file register file) using SIDN as an unchecked index. The PR removes the previously mandatory trap-on-invalid-SIDN behavior (illegal instruction on siselect/sireg/stopei access, read-only zero on hgeip/hgeie/hstatus.vgein, SEIP=0), making the invalid-SIDN behavior UNSPECIFIED. If the hardware does not implement bounds-checking comparators on SIDN before using it to index internal state arrays, out-of-bounds reads return uninitialized or stale register state, and out-of-bounds writes corrupt memory adjacent to the array.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: msdcfg.SIDN used as array index without bounds check; SIDN >= NUM_SUPERVISOR_DOMAINS not gated before hgeip/hgeie internal array access; siselect/sireg CSR access path missing SIDN validity check; stopei CSR read path missing SIDN validity gate; IMSIC interrupt file address computation using SIDN without saturation/clamping
security_spec.summary: PR removes mandatory trap-and-zero behavior for invalid msdcfg.SIDN, making hardware-level SIDN bounds-checking critical: missing comparators allow out-of-bounds array indexing into per-domain hgeip/hgeie/IMSIC register state, leaking stale internal state or corrupting adjacent memory

findings.finding: VSEIP computation uses VGEIN as direct bit-index into hgeip.asUInt without any bounds gate: hgeip.asUInt(hstatusVGEIN.asUInt). The HstatusVgeinField WLRL has no legalRange or legalValues defined, so isLegal returns true.B for all 6-bit values (0-63). Writes of VGEIN > 7 are silently accepted, and the bit-extract at the illegal VGEIN index reads from zero-padded bits above the implemented hgeip[7:1] field, producing VSEIP=0 when a valid guest interrupt might be pending.
findings.snippet: regOut.VSEIP := hvip.VSEIP || platformIRP.VSEIP || hgeip.asUInt(hstatusVGEIN.asUInt)

spec_citations.excerpt: The VGEIN (Virtual Guest External Interrupt Number) field selects a guest external interrupt source for VS-level external interrupts. VGEIN is a WLRL field that must be able to hold values between zero and the maximum guest external interrupt number (known as GEILEN), inclusive.

The number of bits implemented in hgeip and hgeie for guest external interrupts is UNSPECIFIED and may be zero. This number is known as GEILEN. ... bits GEILEN:1 shall be writable in hgeie, and all other bit positions shall be read-only zeros in both hgeip and hgeie.

findings.finding: HstatusVgeinField extends CSREnum with WLRLApply but defines NO legalValues or legalRange. The default CSREnum.isLegal returns true.B (all values legal), making the WLRL write gate wen && wfield.isLegal a no-op. Any 6-bit value (0-63) is accepted as a write to VGEIN, despite the spec mandating legal values are only [0, GEILEN]. With geilen=7, values 8-63 are illegally writable.
findings.snippet: object HstatusVgeinField extends CSREnum with WLRLApply

spec_citations.excerpt: Software should not write anything other than legal values to such a field ... Implementations are permitted but not required to raise an illegal-instruction exception if an instruction attempts to write a non-supported value to a WLRL field.

findings.finding: Configuration mismatch: vgeinWidth=6 (encoding 64 values, 0-63) but geilen=7 (only 7 guest domains, legal VGEIN 0-7). The 6-bit field can hold values far exceeding the legal range, and the WLRL isLegal check is width-agnostic (always returns true), so software-controlled VGEIN values 8-63 pass all gates.

IMSICParams: aia.IMSICParams = aia.IMSICParams(
  ...
  geilen = 7,
  vgeinWidth = 6,

findings.finding: Bounds check (vgein===0 || vgein>geilen) properly gates stopei/vstopei illegal-instruction. Correct but critically incomplete: does not prevent unbounded hgeip bit extraction at MachineLevel:285.

findings.finding: statusIO.vgein = UInt(6.W) — 6-bit bus width allows values 0-63 to propagate. With geilen=7, width exceeds needed 3 bits. Enables illegal VGEIN values on internal buses.
SGEIP := Cat(hgeip.asUInt & hgeie.asUInt).orR — full-vector OR-reduction, not VGEIN-indexed. Correct and unaffected by VGEIN bounds issues.
findings.snippet: regOut.SGEIP := Cat(hgeip.asUInt & hgeie.asUInt).orR

findings.finding: Candidate1 uses VGEIN =/= 0 for VS interrupt routing. Illegal VGEIN (e.g. 63) passes =/= 0 check, routing through Candidate1. Functionally benign since vsip.SEIP=0 for VGEIN>7, but logic correctness depends on undefined VGEIN value.
findings.snippet:
val Candidate1 = vsip.SEIP && vsie.SEIE && (hstatus.VGEIN.asUInt =/= 0.U) && (vstopei.asUInt =/= 0.U)
val Candidate2 = vsip.SEIP && vsie.SEIE && (hstatus.VGEIN.asUInt === 0.U) && ...
val Candidate3 = vsip.SEIP && vsie.SEIE && !Candidate1 && !Candidate2
